title: Unissued RCA-Victor sextet sides, "Midnight With Sampson" and "Blues For J.T."
summary: He goes through sextet titles with Marshall Royal and Chico Hamilton, a bossa nova "Perdido", and tunes dedicated to Bill Sampson and J.T. Gibson.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: And here's another thing of my Sextet, with Marshall Royal, Maxwell Davis, Floyd Turner, Eddie Beal, and with Chico Hamilton on drums and Albert Calderone on timbales. This is one where I remember doing "Perdido" bossa-nova style, which was probably way ahead of its time. They didn't release that one. And there were another two things, "Fooled Again" and "Don't Lend Me No Money," unissued on RCA-Victor. "Midnight With Sampson." There was a guy called Bill Sampson who had a disk jockey show that came on at midnight...
Bill used to live in the house where (?) did.

Really. So I dedicated this one, "Midnight With Sampson", and Victor released it. Then another thing I had, "Number Three." I used to write so many Blues-type tunes, I'd just put numbers on them, and this one was called "Number Three." And "(?) and Company." Then I also did "Pastel." That was released on Victor. I had forgotten that one, too. Then "Hollywood Drive" and "Early Times", "Lonesome Rebecca." And one that I really wish they had released was a Mississippi Blues, which would be good even now. It was a real funky Rock-and-Roll type thing. But RCA didn't believe in that at the time, you see. And "Blues For J.T.," that was...
...who was the Theatrical Editor of the Los Angeles Sentinel and a sometime trumpet player.
No, and Gertrude's ex-husband. Or at that time maybe husband.
When I met J.T. in 1948 or '9, they were already divorced.
They were divorced. And a couple of other things, "Loose Pork Chops" and "Blow, Mr. Norris" which featured Chuck Norris on guitar. Do you remember him?
He's still around. And then a lot of "Details Unknown" they say here.
